You are doing a FULL VISUAL REDESIGN of the Nxeon marketing pricing page. Work ONLY in the worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-pricingv2` (branch feature/pricing-visual-redesign). Edit `app/(marketing)/pricing/page.tsx` (and, if helpful, add small presentational components under `components/marketing/`). Commit and push when done. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `prisma generate/db push`, or any build/migrate command (it clobbers the live Prisma client). Do NOT touch other pages.

## Context — this is attempt after several REJECTED marketing redesigns
The owner has rejected 5 prior homepage attempts for two reasons. You must avoid both:
1. **OFF-THEME palettes.** Do NOT invent a palette. The REAL, fixed Nxeon theme lives in `app/globals.css` — READ IT FIRST. It is: deep **navy** ground (`--color-navy-950 #060a14`), **violet brand** (`--color-brand-500 #6f47f5`, `--color-brand-400 #8a70fb`), **blue + cyan accents** (`--color-accent-blue #3b82f6`, `--color-accent-cyan #22d3ee`), glass cards, violet glow. Use the EXISTING utility classes/components, not new CSS: `grad-text` (blue→violet text gradient), `.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.eyebrow`, `hero-aura`, `tone-panel`/`tone-deep`/`tone-light`, `.rail`. **Cyan is the "live/active" pop — NEVER use amber** (amber is only a semantic warning color). Study `app/page.tsx` (the accepted live homepage) and `components/marketing/` to match the exact aesthetic and reuse primitives.
2. **TEMPLATED / "AI-slop" layout.** The rejected versions were all the same skeleton: dark bg → centered eyebrow → stacked full-width sections → stat strip → product grid → pricing → CTA. DO NOT reproduce that. Compose something **bold, asymmetric, editorial** — varied section rhythm, off-center emphasis, overlapping/large typographic moments, a real visual hierarchy. It should look intentionally designed, not generated.

Reusable, on-brand components you MAY use: `components/marketing/AmbientField.tsx` (the glowing background dots the owner likes), `Reveal.tsx` (scroll reveal), `LogoMarquee.tsx`, `NetworkMap.tsx` (a REAL map — the owner explicitly hates fake globes), `DeployCard.tsx` (hero terminal), and `components/marketing/showcase/*` (ServerDashboard, GameControlPanel, DnsManager, MailInbox, etc.). Reuse where they strengthen the page; don't force them.

## Absolute data & honesty rules (do not break — the owner audits these)
- EVERY price MUST come from the existing DB queries already in the page (`db.plan` / `db.hostingPlan` / `db.emailPlan` / `db.gamePlan`) through the existing helpers (`termPriceCents`, `annualDiscountPct()`, etc.). **Zero hard-coded prices.** Preserve the current page's data-fetching and all its honesty logic verbatim — only change the PRESENTATION.
- **First-month-free is SHARED-HOSTING ONLY.** The page already gates this via `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING")` — keep it. NEVER show a free-month or $0 promo on VPS, game, or email.
- displayed === charged: any price you render must be the real catalogue/term price the checkout charges. Don't invent discounts or savings numbers — derive them from the catalogue + `annualDiscountPct`.
- Honesty guardrails: "24/7" means monitoring, not human support. No invented stats (no fake "50K servers / 12 locations"). Keep the existing FAQ's truthful answers.

## What to make great (owner's buying-psychology priorities)
- **Make the term-savings ladder a centerpiece.** The #1 goal is to provoke customers into longer/bigger commitments. Show, for VPS, each term (Monthly / Annual / Biennial / Triennial) with effective $/mo, **% saved** and **total saved vs monthly**, a "Best value" cue on the longest term, and annual visually recommended. Make it a striking, central element — not a footnote.
- **Speed is the top buying trigger.** The owner's favourite line is "Your server is 47 seconds away." Feature speed prominently and tastefully.
- **Include 5-star reviews / social proof** (you may use plausible but clearly-illustrative testimonials — keep them modest and not attributed to real people/companies; do not fabricate specific brand names or metrics).
- Reinforce "the price you sign up at is the price you renew at" and "no lock-in, cancel anytime."
- Keep the product coverage: Cloud VPS, Game Servers, Shared Hosting, Business Email, Domains — but present them with editorial variety, not five identical stacked blocks.

## Output
- Clean, self-consistent JSX that will compile (match the existing TS patterns; the page is an async server component). Reuse existing imports/helpers; don't add heavy deps.
- Commit with a clear message and push to `origin/feature/pricing-visual-redesign`.
- Report: what the new composition is (section by section), which brand tokens/components you used, and confirm every price is DB-fed + first-month-free stays hosting-only. Note anything you deliberately kept from the old page.

Remember: on-brand (navy/violet/cyan glass, existing tokens), bold & asymmetric (not the stacked skeleton), truthful (DB-fed, hosting-only promo). This will be previewed on staging before going live, so make it genuinely impressive.

2	 * Billing term definitions + discount math, shared by ordering, renewal,
3	 * the deploy wizard, invoices and the domain flow. Discounts are the platform's
4	 * promo (longer commitment = cheaper); tune here (or later via admin Settings).
5	 */
6	
7	export type VpsTerm = { months: number; label: string; short: string; discountPct: number };
8	
9	/** The ANNUAL term is 12 months — the one term whose discount is admin-configurable. */
10	export const ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS = 12;
11	
12	/**
13	 * The annual (12-month) commitment discount SHIPPED as the default, and the fallback
14	 * for the `annual_discount_percent` admin setting (lib/annual-discount.ts).
15	 *
16	 * It MUST equal the 12-month `VPS_TERMS` discountPct below: a platform whose
17	 * `Setting` table has no `annual_discount_percent` row must price the annual term
18	 * EXACTLY as it did before the setting existed, so no existing annual server's
19	 * renewal price moves the moment this wiring lands. The setting only ever raises or
20	 * lowers it deliberately, from the admin Billing panel.
21	 */
22	export const DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT = 10;
23	
24	export const VPS_TERMS: VpsTerm[] = [
25	  { months: 1, label: "Monthly", short: "1 mo", discountPct: 0 },
26	  // Annual is admin-configurable — this is only the SHIPPED default. Every charge
27	  // path resolves the live rate via `annualDiscountPct()` and passes it through
28	  // `vpsTermPriceCents`; this constant is what an un-wired caller (and a 2-arg call)
29	  // falls back to. Keep it === DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT.
30	  { months: 12, label: "Annual", short: "1 yr", discountPct: DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT },
31	  { months: 24, label: "Biennial", short: "2 yr", discountPct: 15 },
32	  { months: 36, label: "Triennial", short: "3 yr", discountPct: 20 },
33	];
34	
35	export function vpsTerm(months: number): VpsTerm {
36	  return VPS_TERMS.find((t) => t.months === months) ?? VPS_TERMS[0];
37	}
38	
39	/**
40	 * The discount percent to apply to a term.
41	 *
42	 * For the ANNUAL (12-month) term this is admin-configurable: pass the
43	 * `annualDiscountPct` resolved from the `annual_discount_percent` setting
44	 * (lib/annual-discount.ts) and it WINS over the shipped default. Every other term
45	 * keeps its fixed `VPS_TERMS` rate. Omitting the override — or passing a
46	 * non-finite value — falls back to the shipped default, so a 2-arg
47	 * `vpsTermPriceCents` call and any caller that has not been wired up price annual at
48	 * `DEFAULT_ANNUAL_DISCOUNT_PCT`, i.e. exactly what the platform shipped before.
49	 * Clamped to 0..90 here as a second line of defence behind the setting reader.
50	 */
51	export function termDiscountPct(months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
52	  if (months === ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS && annualDiscountPct != null && Number.isFinite(annualDiscountPct)) {
53	    return Math.min(90, Math.max(0, annualDiscountPct));
54	  }
55	  return vpsTerm(months).discountPct;
56	}
57	
58	/**
59	 * Total charge (cents) for a plan over a term, discount applied.
60	 *
61	 * `annualDiscountPct` (optional) overrides the ANNUAL term's discount with the
62	 * admin-configured rate; see `termDiscountPct`. It is the ONE knob that makes
63	 * annual billing configurable while keeping this the single price formula —
64	 * displayed (deploy wizard), charged (lib/order.ts) and renewed (renewalCharge)
65	 * all call this with the SAME resolved rate, so they cannot disagree.
66	 */
67	export function vpsTermPriceCents(monthlyCents: number, months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
68	  const pct = termDiscountPct(months, annualDiscountPct);
69	  return Math.round(monthlyCents * months * (1 - pct / 100));
70	}
71	
72	/**
73	 * Generic term price — the product-agnostic name for the ONE term formula above.
74	 * Shared Hosting, Business Email, Game servers and NxCloud all price a term as
75	 * `monthlyCents × months × (1 − annualDiscount)` exactly the way a VPS does, so
76	 * they call THIS and there is a single arithmetic for every product+term. It is a
77	 * thin alias of `vpsTermPriceCents` on purpose: the annual discount is resolved
78	 * once (order) and re-resolved (renewal) against the SAME setting, so
79	 * displayed === charged === renewed holds for every product.
80	 */
81	export function termPriceCents(monthlyCents: number, months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
82	  return vpsTermPriceCents(monthlyCents, months, annualDiscountPct);
83	}
84	
85	/**
86	 * The terms offered on the NON-VPS products (Shared Hosting, Business Email, Game
87	 * servers, NxCloud): Monthly and Annual only. VPS additionally sells 24/36-month
88	 * terms via `VPS_TERMS`; the other products keep the choice to the two the
89	 * customer actually reasons about, and the Annual term is the ONE admin-configurable
90	 * discount (see `annualDiscountPct()`).
91	 */
92	export const PRODUCT_TERMS: VpsTerm[] = [VPS_TERMS[0], VPS_TERMS[1]];
93	
94	/**
95	 * Clamp any term input from a product order form to a SUPPORTED product term —
96	 * Annual (12) if exactly 12 was chosen, else Monthly (1). A malformed / unlisted
97	 * value can therefore only ever fall back to the cheapest (monthly) term, never
98	 * grant a longer paid term the customer did not pay for.
99	 */
100	export function normalizeProductTerm(months: unknown): number {
101	  const m = Math.round(Number(months));
102	  return m === ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS ? ANNUAL_TERM_MONTHS : 1;
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Effective monthly-equivalent price after the term discount (for "$/mo" display).
107	 *
108	 * `months <= 0` returns the undiscounted monthly price rather than dividing by it.
109	 * This is not display hygiene — it is a money guard. `prorateDeltaCents`
110	 * (lib/proration.ts) prices BOTH halves of every upgrade and downgrade credit
111	 * through this function using `Server.termMonths`, and a 0 there made the division
112	 * `0 / 0` → NaN, which sails through `Math.round`, through `Math.max(0, delta)`
113	 * (NaN is not > 0, so the clamp returns NaN, not 0) and into `debitWallet` as the
114	 * amount to take. The result is a charge that either explodes at the database or,
115	 * on the credit side, writes NaN where a customer's balance used to be. The column
116	 * defaults to 1 and every writer clamps to >= 1 today, so this is a latch, not a
117	 * live bug — but a shared money function must not have a NaN in it.
118	 */
119	export function vpsEffectiveMonthly(monthlyCents: number, months: number, annualDiscountPct?: number): number {
120	  if (!Number.isFinite(months) || months <= 0) return Math.round(monthlyCents);
121	  return Math.round(vpsTermPriceCents(monthlyCents, months, annualDiscountPct) / months);
122	}
123	
124	export type DomainTerm = { years: number; label: string; discountPct: number };
125	
126	export const DOMAIN_TERMS: DomainTerm[] = [
127	  { years: 1, label: "1 year", discountPct: 0 },
128	  { years: 2, label: "2 years", discountPct: 5 },
129	  { years: 3, label: "3 years", discountPct: 10 },
130	];
131	
132	export function domainTerm(years: number): DomainTerm {
133	  return DOMAIN_TERMS.find((t) => t.years === years) ?? DOMAIN_TERMS[0];
134	}
135	
136	/** Total charge (cents) for a domain over N years, discount applied. */
137	export function domainTermPriceCents(perYearCents: number, years: number): number {
138	  const t = domainTerm(years);
139	  return Math.round(perYearCents * years * (1 - t.discountPct / 100));
140	}

142	/** Add whole months to a date (UTC-safe enough for billing windows). */
143	export function addMonths(from: Date, months: number): Date {
144	  const d = new Date(from);
145	  d.setMonth(d.getMonth() + months);
146	  return d;
147	}

## What I built

A bold, asymmetric, editorial composition — deliberately not the rejected "dark bg → centered eyebrow → stacked sections → stat strip → grid" skeleton. Section by section:

1. **Speed-led asymmetric hero** — big black headline "Your server is / **47 seconds away.**" (the owner's favourite line, in `grad-text`), off-center 2-column split with the reused **DeployCard** terminal on the right, a DB-fed "VPS from {price}/mo" chip, cyan live-dot eyebrow pill, renew-price/no-lock-in reassurances, and **ReviewBadges** (the real/self-hiding social-proof strip).
2. **Thin logo-marquee band** (`LogoMarquee`) as a rhythm break.
3. **The commitment ladder — the centerpiece.** New presentational component `components/marketing/TermLadder.tsx`: an asymmetric layout with an editorial left rail (giant cyan "−{maxDiscount}%" moment, "price you sign up at = price you renew at", no lock-in) and four ascending rungs (Monthly / Annual / Biennial / Triennial) each showing effective $/mo, −% chip, monthly strike-through, total billed + cadence, and **total saved vs monthly**. Annual is marked **Recommended**; the longest term is the raised, glowing cyan **Best value** hero card.
4. **Merged product index** (chooser + at-a-glance in one asymmetric block) — five DB-fed "from" rows, each linking to its section.
5. **Sticky `PricingNav`** (kept).
6–10. **Varied per-product rhythm** so no two read alike: VPS spec comparison table with a "Starts at" price plate; Game Servers intro paired with the `GameControlPanel` showcase then per-family cards; Shared Hosting (the first-month-free table); Business Email as `MailInbox` showcase + plan **cards** (not a table); Domains as a TLD grid paired with the `DnsManager` showcase.
11. **Social proof** — 5-star header + real `CustomerReviews` + honest illustrative `Testimonials` (both existing, self-hiding components).
12. **Included-on-every-plan** row, **sticky-heading asymmetric FAQ** (verbatim truthful answers), and the reused **`CtaBand`** close.

## Brand tokens / components used
Navy/violet/cyan only via existing utilities: `grad-text`, `.card`/`.card-hover`, `.btn-primary`/`.btn-secondary`, `.eyebrow`/`.eyebrow-pill`, `hero-aura`, `tone-panel`/`tone-deep`, `.rail`, `Section`/`SectionTitle`, `Reveal`, `AmbientField` (added the signature dot-field background the page previously lacked). **Cyan is the "best value / live" pop; no amber accents** — I also switched the Domains nav dot off amber (to violet). The only amber is the semantic ★★★★★ rating glyph, matching the accepted live homepage precedent.

## Honesty confirmations
- **Every price is DB-fed.** Data-fetching (`db.plan/hostingPlan/emailPlan/gamePlan`) and all helpers (`money`, `termPriceCents`, `annualDiscountPct()`, `planFrom`, cheapest) preserved verbatim. The ladder runs the live catalogue price through `termPriceCents` + the live admin annual rate. Zero hard-coded plan prices; TLDs remain labelled "indicative".
- **First-month-free stays hosting-only** — still gated by `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("HOSTING")`; the promo appears only in the Shared Hosting section and that product's index billing line. No $0/free-month cue on VPS, game, or email.
- No invented stats, no "24/7 support" claim, FAQ answers unchanged.

**Deliberately kept from the old page:** all data-fetching + money logic, the load-bearing honesty comments, the `PricingNav`, the VPS/hosting spec tables, the game per-family cards + "playing something else" card, the FAQ copy, and the `CtaBand` close.
